source.title: Mechanistic Interpretability in the Presence of Architectural Obfuscation

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It tests indirect-object identification and the roles of components using attribution and activation patching, but does not reproduce the original circuit’s full 26-head analysis or its faithfulness, completeness and minimality tests.
record.gate_note: The paper reports qualitative results for IOI attribution and patching in a standard GPT-2 small model and a custom obfuscated GPT-2-small model. It does not report a complete circuit ablation or test the original circuit criteria. Numerical values visible only in figures are not transcribed as numbers. HellaSwag and claims cited from other papers are not rows.
record.test_reason: On GPT-2 small's IOI task, logit attribution and activation patching (not the original path patching or ablation criteria) recover the layer-9 positive heads (9.6, 9.9), the negative heads 10.7 and 11.10, and the S2-to-END pathway. A from-scratch, permuted-tokenizer GPT-2-small gives a new-model comparison bearing on V3.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that the S2-to-END circuit survives obfuscation, while activations become diffuse, late-block roles invert, and head importance scatters, which hinders fine-grained interpretation but leaves accuracy intact. The abstract claims 'quantitative evidence', but the results are reported qualitatively. The attention-head ablation promised in the abstract is not reported.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the IOI task and activation patching, but studies a custom seeded-tokenizer obfuscation and does not reproduce the original full circuit discovery, ablation, or faithfulness, completeness and minimality tests.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported account varies by analysis: logit attribution describes broadly similar head behavior across models, while component and head patching describe redistributed or less consistent head roles in the obfuscated model. The study does not systematically vary ablation type, metric, or prompt distribution.
record.problems: The reported patching and attribution findings are qualitative, with no numerical effect sizes or uncertainty estimates in the text. The paper does not test a complete circuit ablation or the original circuit criteria. The obfuscated model is a custom model trained from scratch, so its results are not a direct comparison of the same checkpoint before and after obfuscation.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for each layer or head beyond the groups explicitly described in the text; figures provide visual detail but the paper does not state their numeric values in text. No results from cited studies or the unrelated HellaSwag evaluation are included.

untested.parts: The full 26-head, 7-class circuit; S-inhibition, induction and duplicate-token head classes; faithfulness, completeness and minimality.
Entire version: no name-mover ablation and no test for backup heads.
Other sizes, training checkpoints, and reuse of components for other tasks. Only one same-size model trained from scratch is tested.
Entire version: no matched comparison of circuit-finding methods, ablation types or metrics.
Entire version: ablation type, metric and prompt distribution are not varied.
Entire version: results are averaged over 8 prompts with no split by name order or template, and no prompts with more names.

missing.what: IOI accuracy or clean logit difference for either model. The paper says performance is preserved but gives no number.
Numeric head and layer effect sizes, visible only in figures

record.verdict_notes: The obfuscated model is trained from scratch on Fineweb-Edu, so it is a different model from the base and is mapped to V3. The paper is internally inconsistent: Section IV-B says the two models show no difference at head level, while head patching shows that 9.6 and 9.9 lose their roles. The paper also mislabels the S2 token as the indirect object. None of the results come with uncertainty estimates.

versions.untested_parts: The full 26-head, seven-class circuit, the named head classes, and the authors’ faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria are not tested as such.
No ablation of main name-mover heads followed by a test for backup-head takeover.
No circuit comparison across other model sizes or training checkpoints, or test of component reuse for other tasks.
No systematic comparison of circuit recovery across ablation types, metrics, or independent circuit-finding methods under matched conditions.
The study compares base and obfuscated models and uses several attribution and patching analyses, but does not systematically vary ablation type, metric, or prompt distribution.
The patching analysis averages over eight prompts, but does not report results separately by name order or template, and does not test prompts with more names.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small model
rows.operation_detail: Logit attribution by layer on the IOI task
rows.measure: Layer contributions to the logit difference
rows.value: Layers 1 through 6 are described as minimal or noisy; layer 7 is where meaningful computation begins; layer 9 has the highest positive contribution; layers 10 and 11 contribute negatively.
rows.note: Qualitative description; no numeric contribution values are stated in the text.
rows.check: Layer-level attribution only. Peak at layer 9 and negative layers 10–11 fit the original, but this does not show the full circuit. No numbers. V4/V5 links removed: no method or ablation comparison.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small model
rows.operation_detail: Attention-head logit attribution on the IOI task
rows.measure: Head contributions to the logit difference
rows.value: Heads 9.6 and 9.9 are identified as the main positive contributors; heads 10.7 and 11.10 contribute negatively.
rows.note: The paper relates these to name-mover and negative name-mover heads, but does not establish the full proposed head classes or circuit.
rows.check: Heads 9.6/9.9 positive and 10.7/11.10 negative match the original's name-mover and negative name-mover heads. Only these heads are named. V4/V5 links removed.

rows.subject: custom GPT-2-small model
rows.operation_detail: Logit attribution by layer and head on the IOI task
rows.measure: Layer and head contributions to the logit difference
rows.value: The paper says the overall head-behavior pattern broadly resembles the standard model, while neuron activations differ; it also says the same heads have similar influence.
rows.note: This is the paper’s logit-attribution account; its later head-patching discussion reports less consistent roles for the key layer-9 heads.
rows.check: This is a different model trained from scratch, so it bears on V3, not V1. Claiming that the same head indices (9.6, 9.9) keep their roles in an independently trained model is implausible, and it conflicts with the paper's own head-patching (r9). No numbers.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small model
rows.operation_detail: Residual-stream denoising patching at layer and token positions

conditions.value: eight prompts; metric averaged over them

rows.measure: Relative change in logit difference after patching
rows.baseline: corrupted-run logit difference; numeric value not stated
rows.value: The second subject token is described as the initial information site; information transfers to the final token. Most computation is said to conclude by layer 8, with layers 9–11 largely preserving the representation.
rows.note: The paper reports a localized path, not a test of the complete 26-head circuit.
rows.check: The S2-to-END residual flow fits the original. The paper mislabels the second subject token as the indirect object 'Mary'. Averaged over 8 prompts with no breakdown by prompt, so it cannot bear on V6. V4 link removed.

rows.subject: custom GPT-2-small model
rows.operation_detail: Residual-stream denoising patching at layer and token positions

conditions.value: eight prompts; metric averaged over them

rows.measure: Relative change in logit difference after patching
rows.baseline: corrupted-run logit difference; numeric value not stated
rows.value: The second subject token and transfer to the final token remain identifiable, but the signal is more diffuse; later layers 9–11 continue modifying the representation.
rows.note: The authors describe the pathway as recognizable but less sharp and more distributed than in the base model.
rows.check: Obfuscated from-scratch model, so the row bears on V3, not V1/V5/V6. The pathway is recognizable but more diffuse, with late layers still active.

source_check.locator_found: IV-C.1, Figure 5; lines 675–769. Eight-prompt averaging: lines 681–690.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small model
rows.operation_detail: Patching at attention input, attention output, and MLP output
rows.measure: Relative change in logit difference after component patching
rows.baseline: corrupted-run logit difference; numeric value not stated
rows.value: The text describes activity around the second subject token in early layers, contributions at the final token in layers 8 and 9, and minimal MLP impact except for MLP0.
rows.note: The authors characterize layers 7–9 as the computational backbone, but do not test the full circuit criteria.
rows.check: Component patching at layer level only; it does not identify head classes. V4 link removed.

rows.subject: custom GPT-2-small model
rows.operation_detail: Patching at attention input, attention output, and MLP output
rows.measure: Relative change in logit difference after component patching
rows.baseline: corrupted-run logit difference; numeric value not stated
rows.value: Layers 8, 9, and 10 gain importance; their contributions at the final token are described as negative, counterbalanced by positive contributions at the second subject token. The text also reports a reversal between earlier and later attention-head contributions.
rows.note: MLP0 is again described as the only MLP with significant influence.
rows.check: Obfuscated model: attention layers 8–10 are negative at END and the contribution of early versus late heads is reversed. Bears on V3, not V1/V4/V5.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small model
rows.operation_detail: Individual attention-head patching at selected layers and token positions
rows.measure: Head-patching contribution to the final logit difference
rows.baseline: corrupted-run logit difference; numeric value not stated
rows.value: Heads 9.9 and 9.6 have strong positive contributions; heads 10.7 and 11.10 contribute negatively. Heads 3.0 and 5.5 are described as weak final contributors with behavior consistent with primitive operations.
rows.note: The study gives qualitative roles for selected heads rather than testing all heads or the stated seven classes.
rows.check: Head patching recovers 9.9/9.6 as positive and 10.7/11.10 as negative. Roles for 3.0 and 5.5 are speculative. The paper does not state whether noising or denoising was used. V4 link removed.

rows.subject: custom GPT-2-small model
rows.operation_detail: Individual attention-head patching at selected layers and token positions
rows.measure: Head-patching contribution to the final logit difference
rows.baseline: corrupted-run logit difference; numeric value not stated
rows.value: Heads 9.9 and 9.6 no longer show a consistent positive signal; negative contributions are described as more frequent and larger across a broader range of heads, particularly in later layers.
rows.note: The paper interprets this as a redistribution of head roles under obfuscation.
rows.check: In the obfuscated model, 9.9 and 9.6 lose their consistent positive signal and negative heads spread more widely. Bears on V3, not V1/V4/V5.

relationships.condition: Standard GPT-2 small, logit attribution and activation patching on 8 IOI prompts
relationships.reason: Recovers name-mover-like heads 9.6/9.9, negative heads 10.7/11.10, and S2-to-END flow concentrated in layers 7–9 (r1, r2, r4, r6, r8). Only a subset of the circuit is tested.
relationships.display_finding: The analysis recovered name-mover-like heads 9.6 and 9.9, negative heads 10.7 and 11.10, and second-subject-to-final-token flow concentrated in layers 7–9, testing a subset of the circuit.
